newsitem.title: JAPAN: Matsumotokiyoshi seen undaunted by drugstore rival.
newsitem.headline: Matsumotokiyoshi seen undaunted by drugstore rival.

text.p: Fast growth at Japanese drugstore giant Matsumotokiyoshi Co Ltd is likely to continue, analysts say, even as a rival venture involving high-powered Japanese and U.S. retailers takes aim at the domestic market.

Investors have rewarded Matsumotokiyoshi's strategy of aggressive expansion, which defied the dull outlook for Japan's economy, by pushing its share price on the over-the-counter market on Friday to 4,140 yen ($33), a new high for this year and up sharply from 3,820 ($31) at the previous day's close.

The drugstore chain on Thursday surprised the market with a much larger than expected upward revision in its earnings forecast, predicting that parent current profits would jump to 6.68 billion yen ($54.7 million) in the year to March 31, 1997 from 4.39 billion yen ($35.9 million) last year.
The company had earlier predicted a profit of 5.30 billion yen ($43.4 million) in fiscal 1996/97.

Analysts expected the company to continue opening new outlets at a rapid pace and perceived little threat from a joint venture announced earlier this week that included a number of big-name retailers.

FamilyMart Co Ltd, a major Japanese operator of convenience stores, said on Wednesday that it and five other Japanese firms, including the giant trade house Itochu Corp, had set up a drugstore venture aiming to have 500 member drugstores in Japan by 2002.
U.S. drug retailer Walgreen Co will provide technical assistance to the venture, with an option to purchase a stake in the future.
The venture, RX Network Inc, aims to take advantage, with Walgreen's expertise, of the move in Japan toward greater dispensing of prescription drugs at drugstores rather than at hospitals.
Only 20 percent of drugstores in Japan currently sell prescription medicines, but the Health and Welfare Ministry has plans to boost that to 30 percent by the year 2000.
Matsumotokiyoshi does not dispense prescription drugs at its outlets.
But analysts said the new venture was unlikely to pose a threat to Matsumotokiyoshi for many years to come.

They said Japan's medical industry is far too regulated to encourage newcomers from different business spheres, who were not likely to be keen about shelling out vast amounts of capital to build their own pharmacies.
"The concept that all drugstores can fill prescriptions must become widespread before Walgreen can do business in Japan," said Noriko Takahashi, an analyst at UBS Securities.
"It would take at least 10 years for Walgreen to start up business here, and until then Matsumotokiyoshi and other drugstore chains should be unaffected," she added.

Ryuichi Tachino, an analyst at Yamaichi Research Institute, said Matsumotokiyoshi plans to open 60 new outlets in fiscal 1997/98, up from 47 new outlets in the previous year. It currently has 273 outlets.
This expansion, he added, would boost the company's sales in 1997/98 to 150 billion yen ($1.22 billion) and its parent current profit to 7.6 billion yen ($62.2 million).
